novel_features.name: Dawn-patrol one-shot
novel_features.description: One spot's next few hours as a paddle/no-paddle line readout: swell, wind, tide and rating joined per hour.
novel_features.rationale: Joins wave, swells, wind, tides and rating on the shared unix timestamp into a single readout no individual API call returns.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs a go/no-go answer for one break without parsing five separate forecast payloads.

novel_features.name: Multi-spot rank
novel_features.description: Score and sort several spots best-first on a transparent sum of wave, wind and swell optimalScore.
novel_features.rationale: Surfline's real side-by-side comparison is web-only and unsorted; this ranks a batch in one /kbyg/spots/batch call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to pick today's best break from a set instead of opening N forecast pages.

novel_features.name: Optimal-window scanner
novel_features.description: Emit only the contiguous time blocks where wave, wind and swell optimalScore are all good, daylight-only.
novel_features.rationale: Walks the forecast horizon and intersects optimalScore blocks with sunlightTimes; no endpoint answers 'when exactly is it good'.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to find the good time slots at one spot without eyeballing an hourly graph.

novel_features.name: Raw conditions dump
novel_features.description: Pipe-friendly table/JSON of min/max/optimalScore/humanRelation plus swell components and wind directionType/gust, no rating editorializing.
novel_features.rationale: Exposes the underlying numeric fields the wrappers fetch but never surface cleanly, for people who distrust the star rating.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs raw numbers to feed its own scoring instead of a pre-judged rating.

novel_features.name: Scriptable alert rules
novel_features.description: Store swell/wind/tide threshold rules locally; alert run fetches a fresh forecast, evaluates them, prints matches and sets an exit code for cron.
novel_features.rationale: Official Surfline alerts are Premium-and-iOS-only; this is a local rule engine over synced forecasts that any cron can drive.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this in unattended/cron contexts to get a nonzero exit when conditions a user defined are met.

novel_features.name: Buoy vs forecast cross-check
novel_features.description: Show nearby-buoy observed swell against the spot's wave forecast for the same window, side by side.
novel_features.rationale: Joins /kbyg/buoys/nearby observations with the spot's wave forecast so you can sanity-check the model against reality.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to tell whether the forecast is tracking the actual buoy readings before trusting it.

novel_features.name: Forecast-history journal
novel_features.description: Snapshot the current forecast into local SQLite and review a spot's snapshots over time.
novel_features.rationale: The API keeps no personal history; local snapshots keyed by spotId+timestamp build the journal the apps don't provide.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to review how a spot's forecast has read over the past days from your own captures.

novel_features.name: Offline spot search
novel_features.description: Resolve spot names to spotIds via FTS over the locally-synced taxonomy, with no network.
novel_features.rationale: After a taxonomy sync, name lookups run entirely against the local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to turn a spot name into an ID before calling forecast commands, even offline.

narrative.headline: Every Surfline forecast, scriptable from your terminal — plus multi-spot ranking, a local forecast journal, and cron-able alerts no Surfline tool has.
narrative.value_prop: Pulls wave, swell, wind, tide, weather, conditions and rating straight from Surfline's API over a browser-fingerprint transport that clears Cloudflare. The differentiators live in the local SQLite store: 'rank' scans a set of spots and sorts them best-first (Surfline's own comparison is web-only), 'now' collapses one spot's next hours into a paddle/no-paddle readout, 'windows' finds the daylight blocks worth surfing, and 'alert run' evaluates your own threshold rules for cron.
narrative.auth_narrative: Basic forecasts, search, taxonomy and multi-spot data need no auth at all (up to a 6-day horizon). For 7–17 day forecasts and premium cams, set a Surfline access token: run 'surfline-pp-cli auth login' with your Surfline email and password (it uses the community password-grant flow against /trusted/token), or 'surfline-pp-cli auth set-token <token>' if you already have one. The token is stored locally and sent as the accesstoken query param; SURFLINE_ACCESS_TOKEN is also honored.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the binary, transport and (optional) token wiring before anything hits the network.
Look up a spot by name online to get its spotId.
Dawn-patrol readout for one spot's next hours.
Rank a set of spots best-first to pick where to go.

troubleshoots.fix: Update to a build that ships the Surf (Chrome TLS) transport; run 'surfline-pp-cli doctor' to confirm the transport is browser-chrome.
Set a token: 'surfline-pp-cli auth login' or 'surfline-pp-cli auth set-token <token>'. 7–17 day horizons are premium-gated.
Offline 'search' indexes spots you've captured with 'journal log'. Run 'surfline-pp-cli journal log <spotId>' first, or use the online 'surfline-pp-cli spots find <name>'.
Use 'surfline-pp-cli search "<name>"' to get the 24-char spotId, then pass it to forecast commands.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or script needs Surfline forecast data as structured output: checking whether one break is worth surfing, ranking several spots to choose between them, finding the good daylight windows, or evaluating user-defined surf-condition alerts on a schedule. It is the right tool when you want raw swell/wind/tide numbers rather than a star rating, or a local history of how forecasts read over time.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to watch live cam video — it returns cam still/stream/rewind URLs, not a video stream.
Do not use it for global non-Surfline weather or for spots Surfline doesn't cover; use a weather API instead.
Do not use it to book sessions, post to Surfline, or manage a Surfline account — it is read-only forecast tooling.
Do not rely on >6-day forecasts without a premium token; those horizons are gated.

recipes.title: Pick today's break from your favorites
recipes.explanation: Batch-fetches all spots and sorts them best-first on combined optimalScore.

recipes.title: Narrow a deep wave payload to the fields you need
recipes.explanation: The wave response is deeply nested; dotted --select pulls just surf height and the swell period/direction so agents don't parse tens of KB.

recipes.title: Find when it's actually good this week
recipes.explanation: Emits only the daylight blocks where wave, wind and swell optimalScore all clear the bar.

recipes.title: Cron a surf alert
recipes.explanation: Evaluates your stored threshold rules against a fresh forecast and exits nonzero when one matches, so cron/CI can act on it.

recipes.title: Sanity-check the forecast against buoys
recipes.explanation: Puts observed nearby-buoy swell next to the spot's forecast swell for the same window.

when is it good to surf this week
